origin.audio: Last night at the film club, Carlos recommended an old black-and-white drama. In the key scene, an old woman opens a cupboard, takes out a coat and smells it, and the camera stays on her for almost a minute. Sara objected that such a slow scene is too much, and Carlos replied that he saw her point, but that the long silence is what makes the loss feel real. By the end of the night, three members had promised to rewatch it.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención en el cineclub: recomienda, describe la escena y responde.

answer.text: I would recommend The Last Lighthouse to anyone who likes quiet stories, because it is worth watching twice. In the key scene, an old man climbs to the top of the lighthouse, sits down and says nothing for ten seconds. What makes the moment so moving is the silence: we understand his whole life without a single word. It is the small detail of his empty hands that conveys his sadness. Sara, I see your point about the pace, and to be fair, the first hour is slow. Even so, I would argue that the slow opening is exactly what makes the ending hit so hard. The performances stand out, and I think the film will hold up when you rewatch it. Overall, it is well worth your time, and I hope that you will all give it a chance.
accepted: I would recommend The Last Lighthouse to anyone who likes quiet stories, because it is worth watching twice. What makes the moment so moving is the silence: we understand his whole life without a single word. It is the small detail of his empty hands that conveys his sadness. Sara, I see your point about the pace, and to be fair, the first hour is slow. Even so, I would argue that the slow opening is exactly what makes the ending hit so hard. The performances stand out, and I think the film will hold up when you rewatch it. Overall, it is well worth your time, and I hope that you will all give it a chance.

I recommend The Last Lighthouse to the whole club because it is worth seeing more than once, and I think that it will surprise you. In the key scene, an old man reaches the top of the lighthouse, sits down and says nothing for ten seconds. What I liked most was the silence, which conveys his whole life without a word. It is the empty chair beside him that shows his sadness. Sara, fair enough, the pace is slow at the start, and I see your point. But I would argue that the slow opening is the reason the ending works so well. The performances stand out, and the film will hold up when you rewatch it. Overall, I would strongly recommend it, and I would gladly talk about it again next week.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención recomienda con una razón, describe la escena en presente con énfasis y responde a la objeción reconociéndola antes de contraargumentar.
